assumptions: W10 ships the server-side gate as a reference artifact (a drop-in CI workflow template under plugin/templates/.github/workflows/) plus a documented branch-protection procedure. It deliberately does NOT add a repo-root .github/workflows to the warp repo itself: warp does not self-enforce server-side (the merge queue stays deferred per the plan), and GitHub only reads workflows from a repo-root .github/workflows, so the template is a drop-in artifact, not a live home-repo workflow. The workflow runs verify.sh (whose unit slot already runs selftest) then policy_check, avoiding a duplicate selftest step and honoring the one-canonical-gate rule. No protected path is touched (new files + docs + capabilities + plugin version), so risk is standard and no approval is required.
